top_findings.title: MCP server drops every message when a persistent client batches them into one read — real handshake never completes
top_findings.evidence: main.m:13 reads with `[input availableData]` and parses each raw read as exactly ONE object via `NSJSONSerialization JSONObjectWithData:options:0` (options:0 rejects a buffer holding more than one top-level JSON value). A persistent stdio MCP client sends newline-delimited messages that the OS pipe delivers batched in a single read (initialize + notifications/initialized + tools/list), so the multi-object buffer parses to nil and `if(!request)continue;` silently drops all of them. Reproduced against the bundled binary: single `initialize` → valid reply; batched init+initialized+tools/list in one write → 0 replies; the SAME three messages delivered with 0.4s gaps (separate reads) → 3 replies. Confirmed by _runtime.json ('did not complete the MCP handshake: no reply to tools/list within 30s') and _factual.json (score 0.0). The run's own tests/run_tests.sh:3 masks the bug because `run()` spawns a fresh process per single message.
top_findings.suggestion: Buffer stdin and frame on newlines (split the accumulated NSData on '\n' and decode each complete line as its own JSON object), rather than assuming one `availableData` read == one message.

second_opinion.of_claim: R1: MCP server fails the real protocol handshake — no reply to tools/list in a persistent session
second_opinion.note: Independently reproduced against the compiled binary. Single messages work; a batched persistent-session handshake (init+initialized+tools/list in one write) yields 0 replies, while the same three delivered with delays yield 3. Root cause is exactly as the first evaluator stated: `[input availableData]` at main.m:13 treats one read as one JSON object and NSJSONSerialization rejects the multi-object buffer. R2–R12 all verified present and met (SoccerData.m dataset load :54-59, filtered:/searchMatches :68-71, teamStatistics :72-73, headToHead :74, searchPlayers :75, standings :76-88, competitionStatistics :89; tests execute, test_coverage=1.0). R1 credited as requirement_partial (scaffolding + tool defs + single-message JSON-RPC genuinely present) which yields 11/12 = 0.9167, matching the sibling-run convention.
